blocks.text: Fist hit the pad once and came back level.
Seth kept it braced against his chest. He waited for the little dip that had followed Fist's turns since the escape from the basement.
It did not come.

Fist hovered a few feet away, watching Billy instead of the pad. The seam at his white cuff had closed. Scuffs still crossed the red leather, but he no longer needed the folded towel beneath him when he slept.
Billy crouched to inspect the cuff.
“Pulling anywhere?”
“No.”
“One more.”
Fist struck, turned and stopped beside Seth's shoulder.
Jenny lowered the watch she had borrowed from the operations desk. During the past week, they had kept these sessions short. Today Fist had stayed steady through every turn.
Seth lowered the pad.
“You've been waiting to do that.”
“I've been waiting for you to stop looking worried afterward.”
Billy straightened. “I still get to look.”
From the operations room, the police-band radio broke into speech.
Nobody had to be told to listen.
A bank alarm. A caller reporting two men inside, at least one armed. The street was close enough that Jenny went to the wall map before the dispatcher finished.
Billy wrote down the address and the reported details.
blocks.alt: Billy writes the bank address from the police-band scanner as Seth, Jenny and recovered Fist prepare to leave the facility.

blocks.text: Seth put the pad away from the doorway. Jenny checked the address over Billy's shoulder. Fist rose beside them, then held himself still.
Billy took his notebook.
“People first.”
They were already moving.
The first police car stood short of the bank, angled toward the curb. An officer was guiding pedestrians back from the glass doors.
Jenny stopped beside him. Billy arrived a moment later, with Seth and Fist behind him.
Through the window, they could see customers crouched near a stone pillar. A masked man with a red scarf stood between them and the front doors. He held a pistol low in one hand.
Farther back, another man in a gray jacket was filling a bag at the teller counter.
Billy looked along the building. A narrow passage ran beside it toward the rear.
“Service exit?” he asked the officer.
“Back alley. Another car's on its way around.”
Seth went to the corner of the passage and looked through. A dark green sedan waited beyond the bank's rear door, its engine running. The driver kept watching that door in his mirror.
He came back far enough to point it out to Billy without calling across the street.
Billy opened his notebook against his palm. On the clean page he drew the front doors, the side passage and the car.
Jenny watched the red-scarfed man turn toward the counter. The nearest customer tried to get up and sank back when the gun moved.
“I can reach his hand,” she said.
Billy looked at the officer. The man checked the customers' position, then nodded.
“I'll cover the front.”

Seth and Fist took the passage. Billy stayed where he could see its mouth and the glass doors. He pointed Jenny toward the nearer door, where the pillar would shelter the customers from the man at the counter.
She waited until Seth had disappeared around the corner.
Then she moved.
The red-scarfed man heard the door open.

By the time he turned, Jenny's white glove had struck his wrist. The pistol hit the floor and slid beneath a bench, away from the customers. She turned his arm behind him and put him down on one knee beside the wall.
The officer entered before the man could pull free.
Jenny let go only when the officer had him.
“Through here,” she told the customers.
The first two were already on their feet. A third had caught the strap of her handbag around the bench leg. Jenny slipped it free and steadied her as she stood.
At the far counter, the man in gray snatched up the money bag.
Jenny kept herself between him and the people crossing the lobby. The stone pillar blocked his direct view of most of them. He backed toward the staff passage instead.
She saw the movement and pointed for Billy through the open door.
He was watching.
blocks.alt: Pink Blur guides customers through the bank’s open front doors after the front robber is disarmed.

blocks.text: The last customer reached the sidewalk with both shoes in one hand. Jenny checked behind the pillar, then moved toward the teller windows.
A woman was crouched beneath the counter. Jenny bent until the woman could see her mask.
“The front door's clear.”
She took the woman’s hand and guided her to the officer at the front door, then doubled back toward the staff passage.
In the alley, Seth had just reached the sedan when the bank's rear door banged open.
The driver saw the gray jacket in his mirror. He lifted one hand from the wheel and waved urgently.
Seth stepped behind the car.
He could hear Fist turning toward the doorway. He kept his own eyes on the sedan. They had each been given something to do.
The engine grew louder. The car began rolling toward the street.
Seth caught the steel rear bumper with both hands and lifted.
The back of the sedan rose. Its rear tires spun above the concrete, throwing grit that had caught in their treads. The front wheels stayed on the ground.
Seth shifted one boot until he had firm footing. The weight pressed down through his arms. He held it steady.
The driver looked over his shoulder.
blocks.alt: Seth holds the rear bumper of the getaway sedan, lifting its driven rear wheels clear of the alley while the driver looks back.

blocks.text: “Switch it off,” Seth said.
The engine roared harder.
Seth did not lift any farther. He thought of the steel drum, the chalk circle and keeping his attention on a job until he had finished it.
At the service door, the robber in gray stopped short of the floating glove.
He had a pistol in his free hand. Fist struck the wrist before he could raise it.
The gun dropped beside the door. Fist swept down and knocked it beneath a fixed metal step. The robber tried to turn back into the bank, but Jenny had reached the inner end of the passage.
blocks.alt: Fist intercepts the gray-jacketed robber’s gun wrist at the bank’s rear service doorway, sending the pistol toward clear pavement.

blocks.text: He looked at Jenny, then at Fist.
The bag slipped from his hand. Bundles of notes spilled against the doorframe.
He raised both hands.
Billy reached the alley mouth as the second police car stopped there. He pointed out the gun beneath the step and the driver in the green sedan.
The officers approached from the car's side. Seth stayed behind it, outside their path.
This time, when an officer told the driver to turn off the engine, he did.
Seth waited until the driver was out and the keys were clear. Then he lowered the rear wheels gently onto the concrete.
One tire made a little squeak as the weight settled.
Fist hovered above the dropped bag.
The officers kept the three men apart while the bank manager checked on the staff.
Billy gave his account and pointed out where both pistols had fallen.
Outside, Jenny checked on the teller. The woman was gripping a little silver pen so tightly that she seemed to have forgotten it was there.
“You can put that down now,” Jenny told her.
The woman looked at her hand, then laughed once in surprise.
Seth waited beside the front doors. He had checked the bumper after lowering the car. The paint had marked his gloves, but nothing on the sedan had come loose.
Fist drifted toward him.
“You didn't need to throw it,” he said.
“I noticed.”
“Getting better at that.”
Seth smiled.
A man who had been crouching behind the pillar came over to thank them. Others followed, talking at once until Billy gently asked them to leave the doorway clear for the officers.
A photographer across the street called for them to look up.
Jenny stayed in her white mask. Seth kept his red one in place. Fist turned toward the camera with the expression of someone who had been ready for it all afternoon.
blocks.alt: Seth, Jenny, Billy and recovered Fist stand outside the bank as relieved civilians thank them and police escort the three suspects away.

blocks.text: Billy closed his notebook and stood beside the others while the photographer lifted his camera.
Seth looked from one face to the next.
They had done what they came to do.
Jenny returned to the bank later in her ordinary clothes.
The doors were locked to customers. She waited while the manager checked her press identification, then asked about the staff, the alarm and what he had seen from behind the counter.
The teller had put down the silver pen. She still twisted her hands together when she described the man with the bag.
Jenny checked the arrests and recovered money with the police before finishing her account at the newspaper office.
The report named the Defenders. It did not name the boy beneath the red mask or connect the white-masked woman to the byline.
The photograph needed no help from the story. All four of them were there outside the bank, with the relieved teller near the door and officers behind them.
At the facility that evening, Claude telephoned Billy after hearing about the arrests.
He did not ask how much of the new equipment they had used. He asked whether everyone had come back safely.

Billy looked through the operations-room doorway. Seth was putting away the training pad. Jenny had brought sandwiches, and Fist was telling her which part of the afternoon the photographer had missed.
“All of us,” Billy said.
Daniel unfolded the next day's newspaper across a workbench.
The photograph occupied the space above Jenny's account. The caption named Super Zerdo, Pink Blur, Inspector Billy and Fist-O-Mite.
He read the report, then returned to the photograph.

Luke hovered at the end of the bench. Behind him, the collector's glass held a faint remnant of orange light from another small test. Daniel had spent the morning making adjustments instead of discussing the newspaper.
“The glove's back,” Luke said.
Daniel examined the repaired cuff in the photograph.
“And they didn't need the flame.”
“No mention of him.”
Daniel studied the four allies in the photograph, then looked at the empty space beside them.
blocks.alt: Daniel studies the bank-robbery report beside Luke in the workshop, considering the coordinated Defenders while the collector waits behind them.

blocks.text: Luke moved nearer the photograph. He remembered the glove coming at him above the roofs, damaged and still refusing to go away.
“You want to fight that lot?”
“No.”
Daniel laid the paper beside the collector. The glass and copper took up most of the bench behind it.
“We'll choose somewhere they aren't.”
He looked toward the brass mouth, then at the space in front of it.
Luke followed his gaze.
